subject: Hosted API: peak surge & monthly burn qualification - Helium AI
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@heliumai.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + hosted pricing inputs (Helium AI)

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the qualification items we discussed so procurement has what they need: 

Summary from Helium's side (please confirm):
- Expected monthly token volume: baseline 120M tokens/month with a likely ramp to 300M/mo in Q3 if pilot looks good.
- Conservative committed ask for pricing: 300M tokens/month.
- Burst/peak profile: short bursts up to ~220 TPS for ~30-90s during query-heavy events; sustained 99th pct at ~60 TPS.
- Target $/1M tokens (customer expectation): roughly $500–$900 range (you mentioned $750 as the target in the demo).

Attachments: I included a short traffic snapshot template (helium-traffic-snapshot.xlsx) for the engineering team to fill in per-endpoint breakdowns — helps us size burst capacity and recommend slab tiers.

Next steps (from Redwood):
1) You confirm the monthly ranges and a procurement contact for DocuSign or PO flow.
2) We’ll send a hosted tier pricing proposal with explicit slab bands + burst SLA options.
3) If Helium is comfortable, we can set up a 7-day sandbox with a test key and a small credits package to validate latency and peak handling.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll aim to send an initial pricing PDF and mutual action plan this afternoon.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Olivia Park <olivia@heliumai.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Helium AI Procurement <procurement@heliumai.io>
Date: 2028-05-02T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + hosted pricing inputs (Helium AI)

Thanks Alex — that looks right overall. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: the 120M baseline is accurate for our current pilot traffic, but if we enable embeddings and more aggressive summarization the practical volume goes up fast. Our internal model shows 450M tokens in month 1 of full feature roll-out and up to ~900M within two quarters. For contracting purposes we want to negotiate on a conservative committed slab of 300M to start.
- Peak TPS: we see very short spikes, sometimes hitting 300 TPS for ~2 minutes during night-batch processing + user ramp. Most customer-facing peaks are 30–90s at 150–220 TPS.
- Budget: procurement gave a $/1M target band of $500–$900; $750 sits in the middle and is acceptable if combined with a 12-month commit and predictable SLOs.

Procurement contact is procurement@heliumai.io — they’ll handle redlines and the PO. I attached our internal token forecast as well (sent separately).

Question: do you support a hosted plan with predictable burst capacity (i.e., we can buy a committed slab and still burst beyond it for short windows with predictable overage pricing)? Also, can you confirm whether sandbox usage counts against the committed slab?

If you can send the pricing bands and a short mutual action plan (who signs what and timing), procurement can respond quickly.

— Olivia Park
Head of Product, Helium AI
olivia@heliumai.io
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@heliumai.io>
Cc: Helium AI Procurement <procurement@heliumai.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted pricing proposal + burst policy (proposal attached)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the detail, that helps a lot. Attached is a short hosted pricing proposal (proposal-heliumai-hosted-pricing.pdf) and a mutual action plan spreadsheet (mutual_action_plan.xlsx). Key highlights below so procurement can skim: 

Pricing summary (hosted API) — preliminary options: 
1) Pay-as-you-go (no commit) — $1,200 / 1M tokens, immediate access, metered monthly. No reserved burst SLA.
2) Committed slab (recommended initial): 300M tokens/month @ $750 / 1M with a 12-month term; includes 10% free KV caching credit and prefix cache tuning. Overage billed at $950 / 1M.
3) Growth slab (volume discount path): >= 1B tokens/month — $650 / 1M with automatic 3% discount step for each additional 1B committed.

Burst policy (hosted): short bursts up to 4x baseline throughput are supported via autoscaling for bursts under 5 minutes; overage pricing applies beyond committed slab but bursts are prioritized if capacity available. We can include a formal burst SLA addendum if Helium needs guaranteed burst capacity windows.

Sandbox note: sandbox keys do not count against the committed slab; we’ll provision a separate test key and include a credits package so you can validate latencies and 99th-quantile TPS behavior.

Requested next steps: 
- Procurement: review attached PDF and MAP, confirm PO owner and preferred contract template (DocuSign link in the MAP).
- Engineering: if you can fill the traffic snapshot we’ll generate a recommended capacity/burst matrix.

I’ll hold a tentative follow-up slot next Wed 10–11AM PT to walk procurement and engineering through the MAP if that helps.

Attachments: proposal-heliumai-hosted-pricing.pdf (pricing summary), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (owner & timeline), heli um-traffic-snapshot.xlsx (template). HubSpot deal link included in the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

— Alex
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T08:00:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Helium AI pricing ask + proposed concession

Internal note — recapping customer signals and recommended concession for Legal/Sales Ops: 
- Customer signals: wants a conservative 300M committed slab, but traffic modeling shows potential for 450–900M in initial rollout. They value predictable cost and burst handling.
- Their budget band centers on $750 / 1M. They asked whether we can provide guaranteed short-burst capacity and whether sandbox counts against commit (we said no).

My recommended concession to close the deal quickly: 
- Offer $725 / 1M for initial 6 months if they sign 12-month 300M/month commit, then revert to $750 for months 7–12.
- Or: $700 / 1M if they commit to escalate to 500M/month within 90 days (firm commitment + PO).
- Include one month of extra credits (equivalent to 10% of committed slab) and a 30-day free trial key that does not count toward committed volume.

Requesting: legal and pricing sign-off on the above options and Sales Ops to confirm DocuSign flow. If we greenlight the $700 path I’ll include it in the MAP and push to procurement.

— Alex
